From fde29fd9349327acc50d19a0b5f3d5a6c964dfd8 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Yiqi Sun <sunyiqixm@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 15:04:19 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] ipv4: icmp: fix null-ptr-deref in icmp_build_probe()

ipv6_stub->ipv6_dev_find() may return ERR_PTR(-EAFNOSUPPORT) when the
IPv6 stack is not active (CONFIG_IPV6=m and not loaded), and passing
this error pointer to dev_hold() will cause a kernel crash with
null-ptr-deref.

Instead, silently discard the request. RFC 8335 does not appear to
define a specific response for the case where an IPv6 interface
identifier is syntactically valid but the implementation cannot perform
the lookup at runtime, and silently dropping the request may safer than
misreporting "No Such Interface".

Fixes: d329ea5bd884 ("icmp: add response to RFC 8335 PROBE messages")
Signed-off-by: Yiqi Sun <sunyiqixm@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260402070419.2291578-1-sunyiqixm@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/ipv4/icmp.c b/net/ipv4/icmp.c
index 568bd1e95d44..4e2a6c70dcd8 100644
--- a/net/ipv4/icmp.c
+++ b/net/ipv4/icmp.c
@@ -1346,6 +1346,13 @@ bool icmp_build_probe(struct sk_buff *skb, struct icmphdr *icmphdr)
 			if (iio->ident.addr.ctype3_hdr.addrlen != sizeof(struct in6_addr))
 				goto send_mal_query;
 			dev = ipv6_stub->ipv6_dev_find(net, &iio->ident.addr.ip_addr.ipv6_addr, dev);
+			/*
+			 * If IPv6 identifier lookup is unavailable, silently
+			 * discard the request instead of misreporting NO_IF.
+			 */
+			if (IS_ERR(dev))
+				return false;
+
 			dev_hold(dev);
 			break;
 #endif
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a null-pointer dereference in `icmp_build_probe()` that can occur when the IPv6 stack is not active. The only file modified is `net/ipv4/icmp.c`.

**Modifications in `net/ipv4/icmp.c`:**
- Added a check after calling `ipv6_stub->ipv6_dev_find()` to test whether the returned pointer is an error (`IS_ERR(dev)`). If so, the function immediately returns `false` (silently discarding the probe request) instead of proceeding to `dev_hold(dev)`, which would crash on an invalid pointer.

**Relationship:**  
The fix introduces a guard condition to handle the case where `ipv6_dev_find()` returns `ERR_PTR(-EAFNOSUPPORT)` (e.g., when `CONFIG_IPV6=m` is not loaded). Previously, this error pointer was passed directly to `dev_hold()`, causing a null-ptr-deref. By returning early, the patch prevents the crash and defers to a safe default behavior (dropping the request) as per RFC 8335 considerations.

Root cause:
The function `icmp_build_probe()` in `net/ipv4/icmp.c` calls `ipv6_stub->ipv6_dev_find()` to look up an IPv6 interface. However, when the IPv6 stack is not active (e.g., `CONFIG_IPV6=m` and not loaded), this function returns `ERR_PTR(-EAFNOSUPPORT)` instead of a valid `struct net_device *`. The code then passes this error pointer directly to `dev_hold(dev)`, which attempts to dereference an invalid address, causing a null-pointer dereference. The root cause is the missing error check after the `ipv6_dev_find()` call.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
dev = ipv6_stub->ipv6_dev_find(net, &iio->ident.addr.ip_addr.ipv6_addr, dev);
dev_hold(dev);
Reason:
`ipv6_stub->ipv6_dev_find()` may return `ERR_PTR(-EAFNOSUPPORT)` when the IPv6 stack is inactive. This error pointer is passed directly to `dev_hold()`, which dereferences it, causing a null-pointer dereference (since `ERR_PTR` is not a valid pointer).

The code statements that fix the bug are:
+			if (IS_ERR(dev))
+				return false;
+
			dev_hold(dev);
Reason:
The added check `IS_ERR(dev)` catches the error pointer returned by `ipv6_stub->ipv6_dev_find()` and returns `false` to silently discard the request, preventing the null-pointer dereference in `dev_hold()`.
